{"content":"# Concurrency test for the two guarantees that make ordering safe under load.
#
#   1. Idempotency  - the same Idempotency-Key submitted 10x in parallel creates exactly one order.
#   2. Slot safety  - different keys racing for the same meal produce exactly one success.
#
# Both are enforced by unique indexes in MySQL, not by application-level locking, so this test
# is meaningful even with several application instances behind a load balancer.
#
#   pwsh -File scripts/concurrency-test.ps1 [-BaseUrl http://localhost:8080] [-Parallel 10]

param(
    [string]$BaseUrl = "http://localhost:8080",
    [int]$Parallel = 10
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Net.Http

$script:Checks = 0
$script:Failures = 0

function Assert-That([string]$Name, [bool]$Condition, [string]$Detail = "") {
    $script:Checks++
    if ($Condition) {
        Write-Host ("  [PASS] " + $Name) -ForegroundColor Green
    } else {
        $script:Failures++
        Write-Host ("  [FAIL] " + $Name + " " + $Detail) -ForegroundColor Red
    }
}

function Section([string]$Title) {
    Write-Host ""
    Write-Host ("== " + $Title) -ForegroundColor Cyan
}

function Invoke-Json {
    param([string]$Method, [string]$Path, [hashtable]$Headers = @{}, $Body = $null)
    $params = @{
        Method      = $Method
        Uri         = $BaseUrl + $Path
        Headers     = $Headers
        UseBasicParsing = $true
    }
    if ($null -ne $Body) {
        $params.ContentType = 'application/json; charset=utf-8'
        $params.Body = ($Body | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10 -Compress)
    }
    try {
        $response = Invoke-WebRequest @params
        $text = if ($response.Content -is [byte[]]) {
            [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetString($response.Content)
        } else { [string]$response.Content }
        return [pscustomobject]@{ Status = [int]$response.StatusCode; Body = ($text | ConvertFrom-Json); Raw = $text }
    } catch {
        $resp = $_.Exception.Response
        if ($null -eq $resp) { throw }
        $reader = New-Object System.IO.StreamReader($resp.GetResponseStream())
        $text = $reader.ReadToEnd()
        $parsed = $null
        try { $parsed = $text | ConvertFrom-Json } catch { }
        return [pscustomobject]@{ Status = [int]$resp.StatusCode; Body = $parsed; Raw = $text }
    }
}

<#
  Fires N requests genuinely in parallel using the .NET HTTP stack, so the server sees
  simultaneous arrivals rather than a sequential loop.
#>
function Invoke-ParallelPosts {
    param(
        [string]$Path,
        [string]$Token,
        [string[]]$IdempotencyKeys,
        [string]$JsonBody
    )
    $handler = New-Object System.Net.Http.HttpClientHandler
    $client = New-Object System.Net.Http.HttpClient($handler)
    $client.Timeout = [TimeSpan]::FromSeconds(60)

    $tasks = @()
    foreach ($key in $IdempotencyKeys) {
        $request = New-Object System.Net.Http.HttpRequestMessage([System.Net.Http.HttpMethod]::Post, ($BaseUrl + $Path))
        $request.Headers.Authorization =
            New-Object System.Net.Http.Headers.AuthenticationHeaderValue("Bearer", $Token)
        $request.Headers.Add("Idempotency-Key", $key)
        $content = New-Object System.Net.Http.StringContent(
            $JsonBody, [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8, "application/json")
        $request.Content = $content
        $tasks += $client.SendAsync($request)
    }

    [System.Threading.Tasks.Task]::WaitAll($tasks)
    $results = @()
    foreach ($task in $tasks) {
        $response = $task.Result
        $body = $response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync().Result
        $parsed = $null
        try { $parsed = $body | ConvertFrom-Json } catch { }
        $results += [pscustomobject]@{
            Status = [int]$response.StatusCode
            Body   = $parsed
            Raw    = $body
        }
    }
    $client.Dispose()
    $handler.Dispose()
    return $results
}

$suffix = [guid]::NewGuid().ToString('N').Substring(0, 8)
$email = "concurrency.$suffix@example.com"
$password = "Passw0rd123"

Section "Setup"
$register = Invoke-Json -Method Post -Path "/api/auth/register" -Body @{
    email = $email; password = $password; displayName = "Concurrency Tester"
}
$token = $register.Body.data.token
$headers = @{ Authorization = "Bearer $token" }
Assert-That "test employee registered" ([bool]$token)

$dates = Invoke-Json -Path "/api/menu/dates" -Headers $headers
$today = $dates.Body.data[0]

# Pick a dish without option groups so the payload needs no configuration.
$menu = Invoke-Json -Path "/api/menu?date=$today&size=50" -Headers $headers
$dish = $menu.Body.data.items | Where-Object { -not $_.hasOptions } | Select-Object -First 1
Assert-That "found a dish without options" ($null -ne $dish)

$orderBody = @{
    items = @(@{ dishId = $dish.dishId; quantity = 2; optionIds = @() })
    deliveryDate = "$today"
    mealSlot = "Lunch"
    deliveryAddress = "Concurrency Lab, Desk 7"
} | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 8 -Compress

Section "Idempotency under $Parallel parallel submissions with the same key"
$sharedKey = [guid]::NewGuid().ToString()
$parallelKeys = @(1..$Parallel | ForEach-Object { $sharedKey })
$sameKeyResults = Invoke-ParallelPosts -Path "/api/orders" -Token $token `
    -IdempotencyKeys $parallelKeys -JsonBody $orderBody

$statuses = $sameKeyResults | ForEach-Object { $_.Status } | Sort-Object -Unique
$orderNos = $sameKeyResults |
    Where-Object { $_.Body -and $_.Body.data } |
    ForEach-Object { $_.Body.data.orderNo } |
    Sort-Object -Unique

Write-Host ("    statuses: " + ($statuses -join ', '))
Write-Host ("    distinct order numbers: " + $orderNos.Count)

Assert-That "every parallel submit succeeded" (($statuses | Where-Object { $_ -ne 200 }).Count -eq 0) `
    "statuses=$($statuses -join ',')"
Assert-That "all $Parallel responses carry the same order number" ($orderNos.Count -eq 1) `
    "orderNos=$($orderNos -join ',')"
Assert-That "exactly one response created the order, the rest are replays" (
    (@($sameKeyResults | Where-Object { $_.Body.data.duplicated -eq $false }).Count) -eq 1)
Assert-That "at least one replay was detected" (
    (@($sameKeyResults | Where-Object { $_.Body.data.duplicated -eq $true }).Count) -ge 1)

$list = Invoke-Json -Path "/api/orders?size=50" -Headers $headers
$created = @($list.Body.data.items | Where-Object { $_.orderNo -eq $orderNos[0] })
Assert-That "the database holds exactly one order for that key" ($created.Count -eq 1) `
    "count=$($created.Count)"
$orderId = $created[0].id

Section "Meal-slot safety: $Parallel different keys racing for the same meal"
$distinctKeys = @(1..$Parallel | ForEach-Object { [guid]::NewGuid().ToString() })
$raceResults = Invoke-ParallelPosts -Path "/api/orders" -Token $token `
    -IdempotencyKeys $distinctKeys -JsonBody $orderBody

$raceStatuses = $raceResults | ForEach-Object { $_.Status } | Group-Object | Sort-Object Name
Write-Host ("    status distribution: " + (($raceStatuses | ForEach-Object { "$($_.Name)x$($_.Count)" }) -join ', '))

$successes = @($raceResults | Where-Object { $_.Status -eq 200 })
$conflicts = @($raceResults | Where-Object { $_.Status -eq 409 })

Assert-That "exactly one racing submit won" ($successes.Count -eq 1) "winners=$($successes.Count)"
Assert-That "every other racing submit got 409" (($successes.Count + $conflicts.Count) -eq $Parallel) `
    "200=$($successes.Count) 409=$($conflicts.Count)"
Assert-That "the conflict reason is ORDER_SLOT_CONFLICT" (
    (@($conflicts | Where-Object { $_.Body.code -eq 'ORDER_SLOT_CONFLICT' }).Count) -eq $conflicts.Count)

$afterRace = Invoke-Json -Path "/api/orders?size=50" -Headers $headers
$forToday = @($afterRace.Body.data.items | Where-Object { $_.status -eq 'Pending' -or $_.status -eq 'Confirmed' })
Assert-That "only one active order exists for the meal" ($forToday.Count -eq 1) "active=$($forToday.Count)"

Section "Slot is released by cancellation"
$activeId = $forToday[0].id
$null = Invoke-Json -Method Post -Path "/api/orders/$activeId/cancel" -Headers $headers
$releaseHeaders = @{ Authorization = "Bearer $token"; "Idempotency-Key" = [guid]::NewGuid().ToString() }
$reorder = Invoke-Json -Method Post -Path "/api/orders" -Headers $releaseHeaders -Body ($orderBody | ConvertFrom-Json)
Assert-That "the meal can be ordered again after cancelling" ($reorder.Status -eq 200) `
    "status=$($reorder.Status)"

Write-Host ""
Write-Host ("=" * 60)
if ($script:Failures -eq 0) {
    Write-Host ("ALL CONCURRENCY CHECKS PASSED (" + $script:Checks + " assertions)") -ForegroundColor Green
    exit 0
} else {
    Write-Host ("FAILED: " + $script:Failures + " of " + $script:Checks + " assertions") -ForegroundColor Red
    exit 1
}

{"content":"# Local infrastructure for WeBox.
#
#   docker compose up -d
#
# Starts the two services the application expects:
#   * MySQL 8 on 3306  - the system of record (standalone server, NOT an embedded database)
#   * Redis 7 on 6379  - a degradable accelerator for the menu cache, order idempotency and
#                        order-number issuance. The application keeps working without it.
#
# If you already run MySQL or Redis locally, skip this file and point the environment
# variables in .env.example at your instances instead.

services:
  mysql:
    image: mysql:8.0
    container_name: webox-mysql
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD: root1234
      MYSQL_DATABASE: webox
      MYSQL_USER: webox
      MYSQL_PASSWORD: webox1234
      TZ: UTC
    command:
      - --character-set-server=utf8mb4
      - --collation-server=utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci
      # Store audit timestamps in UTC; the application also pins hibernate.jdbc.time_zone=UTC.
      - --default-time-zone=+00:00
    ports:
      - "3306:3306"
    volumes:
      - webox-mysql-data:/var/lib/mysql
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "mysqladmin", "ping", "-h", "127.0.0.1", "-uwebox", "-pwebox1234"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 20
      start_period: 30s

  # Creates the integration-test schema next to the main one.
  mysql-init:
    image: mysql:8.0
    depends_on:
      mysql:
        condition: service_healthy
    entrypoint:
      - bash
      - -c
      - >
        mysql -h mysql -uwebox -pwebox1234
        -e "CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS webox_test
        CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci;"
    restart: "no"

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    container_name: webox-redis
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "6379:6379"
    volumes:
      - webox-redis-data:/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "redis-cli", "ping"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10

volumes:
  webox-mysql-data:
  webox-redis-data:
","file_path":"D:\G\MyRep\webox\docker-compose.yml"}

{"content":"# WeBox environment variables.
#
#   cp .env.example .env      (then edit the values)
#
# The backend reads these at startup; every one of them has a working localhost default
# except the JWT secret and the database password.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# MySQL - the system of record. Must be a standalone server (Docker container or a
# locally installed MySQL 8). Embedded databases such as H2 or SQLite are not supported.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
WEBOX_DB_URL=jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/webox?useSSL=false&allowPublicKeyRetrieval=true&serverTimezone=UTC&characterEncoding=UTF-8&useUnicode=true
WEBOX_DB_USERNAME=webox
WEBOX_DB_PASSWORD=webox1234

# Only used by `mvn verify -Pintegration`.
WEBOX_TEST_DB_URL=jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/webox_test?useSSL=false&allowPublicKeyRetrieval=true&serverTimezone=UTC&characterEncoding=UTF-8&useUnicode=true

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Redis - optional accelerator. Leave the password empty for a default Redis.
# If Redis is unavailable the API still works: the menu is read from MySQL, idempotency
# falls back to the database unique index, and order numbers use a random suffix.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
WEBOX_REDIS_HOST=localhost
WEBOX_REDIS_PORT=6379
WEBOX_REDIS_PASSWORD=

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Security. If WEBOX_JWT_SECRET is left empty the application generates an ephemeral key at
# startup and logs a warning: everything works, but restarting invalidates existing tokens.
# Use at least 32 characters in any real deployment.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
WEBOX_JWT_SECRET=
WEBOX_JWT_TTL_HOURS=8
WEBOX_CORS_ORIGINS=http://localhost:5173,http://127.0.0.1:5173

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Application
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
WEBOX_SERVER_PORT=8080
# Decides the 10:00 / 15:00 ordering cut-offs and which calendar day "today" means.
WEBOX_TIME_ZONE=Asia/Shanghai
# Where uploaded dish images are written.
WEBOX_UPLOAD_DIR=./data/uploads
WEBOX_MENU_CACHE_TTL_MINUTES=10

# Seed data (admin account, dish catalog, today's and tomorrow's menu). Idempotent.
WEBOX_SEED_ENABLED=true
WEBOX_SEED_ADMIN_EMAIL=admin@webox.com
WEBOX_SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD=Admin1234
","file_path":"D:\G\MyRep\webox\.env.example"}

content.arguments:
{"content":"# Starts everything needed for a local demo.
#
#   pwsh -File scripts/dev.ps1              # infrastructure must already be running
#   pwsh -File scripts/dev.ps1 -WithDocker  # also runs `docker compose up -d` first
#
# Opens the backend on :8080 and the SPA on :5173 in two windows, waits until both answer,
# then prints the URLs.

param(
    [switch]$WithDocker,
    [string]$JavaHome = $env:JAVA_HOME
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
$root = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot

if ($WithDocker) {
    Write-Host 'Starting MySQL and Redis via docker compose...'
    Push-Location $root
    docker compose up -d
    Pop-Location
}

if (-not $JavaHome -or -not (Test-Path (Join-Path $JavaHome 'bin\java.exe'))) {
    Write-Warning 'JAVA_HOME does not point at a JDK 17 installation. Set it first, e.g.:'
    Write-Warning '  $env:JAVA_HOME = "C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-17.0.2"'
    exit 1
}

# --- backend -------------------------------------------------------------
$backendDir = Join-Path $root 'backend'
$jar = Join-Path $backendDir 'target\webox-backend-1.0.0.jar'

if (-not (Test-Path $jar)) {
    Write-Host 'Building the backend (first run downloads dependencies)...'
    Push-Location $backendDir
    if (Test-Path '.\mvnw.cmd') { & .\mvnw.cmd -B -q package -DskipTests }
    else { & mvn -B -q package -DskipTests }
    Pop-Location
}

Write-Host 'Starting the backend on http://localhost:8080 ...'
Start-Process -FilePath (Join-Path $JavaHome 'bin\java.exe') `
    -ArgumentList '-jar', $jar `
    -WorkingDirectory $backendDir `
    -RedirectStandardOutput (Join-Path $backendDir 'backend.log') `
    -RedirectStandardError (Join-Path $backendDir 'backend.err.log')

# --- frontend ------------------------------------------------------------
$frontendDir = Join-Path $root 'frontend'
if (-not (Test-Path (Join-Path $frontendDir 'node_modules'))) {
    Write-Host 'Installing frontend dependencies...'
    Push-Location $frontendDir
    npm install --no-audit --no-fund
    Pop-Location
}

Write-Host 'Starting the SPA on http://localhost:5173 ...'
Start-Process -FilePath 'npm.cmd' -ArgumentList 'run', 'dev' -WorkingDirectory $frontendDir

# --- wait for readiness --------------------------------------------------
$backendReady = $false
for ($i = 1; $i -le 45; $i++) {
    Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
    try {
        Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'http://localhost:8080/actuator/health' -TimeoutSec 4 -UseBasicParsing | Out-Null
        $backendReady = $true
        break
    } catch { }
}

$frontendReady = $false
for ($i = 1; $i -le 30; $i++) {
    Start-Sleep -Seconds 1
    try {
        Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'http://localhost:5173/' -TimeoutSec 3 -UseBasicParsing | Out-Null
        $frontendReady = $true
        break
    } catch { }
}

Write-Host ''
Write-Host ('backend  : ' + $(if ($backendReady) { 'UP  http://localhost:8080' } else { 'NOT RESPONDING - see backend/backend.log' }))
Write-Host ('frontend : ' + $(if ($frontendReady) { 'UP  http://localhost:5173' } else { 'NOT RESPONDING - see the npm window' }))
Write-Host ''
Write-Host 'Employee app : http://localhost:5173'
Write-Host 'Console      : http://localhost:5173/console'
Write-Host 'API docs     : http://localhost:8080/swagger-ui.html'
Write-Host 'Admin login  : admin@webox.com / Admin1234'
","file_path":"D:\G\MyRep\webox\scripts\dev.ps1"}

#
#   cp .env.example .env      (then edit the values)
#
# The backend reads these at startup; every one of them has a working localhost default
# except the JWT secret and the database password.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# MySQL - the system of record. Must be a standalone server (Docker container or a
# locally installed MySQL 8). Embedded databases such as H2 or SQLite are not supported.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
WEBOX_DB_URL=jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/webox?useSSL=false&allowPublicKeyRetrieval=true&serverTimezone=UTC&characterEncoding=UTF-8&useUnicode=true

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Redis - optional accelerator. Leave the password empty for a default Redis.
# If Redis is unavailable the API still works: the menu is read from MySQL, idempotency
# falls back to the database unique index, and order numbers use a random suffix.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
WEBOX_REDIS_HOST=localhost
WEBOX_REDIS_PORT=6379
WEBOX_REDIS_PASSWORD=

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

{"content":"# Starts everything needed for a local demo.
#
#   pwsh -File scripts/dev.ps1              # infrastructure must already be running
#   pwsh -File scripts/dev.ps1 -WithDocker  # also runs `docker compose up -d` first
#
# Opens the backend on :8080 and the SPA on :5173 in two windows, waits until both answer,
# then prints the URLs.

param(
    [switch]$WithDocker,
    [string]$JavaHome = $env:JAVA_HOME
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
$root = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot

if ($WithDocker) {
    Write-Host 'Starting MySQL and Redis via docker compose...'
    Push-Location $root
    docker compose up -d
    Pop-Location
}

if (-not $JavaHome -or -not (Test-Path (Join-Path $JavaHome 'bin\java.exe'))) {
    Write-Warning 'JAVA_HOME does not point at a JDK 17 installation. Set it first, e.g.:'
    Write-Warning '  $env:JAVA_HOME = "C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-17.0.2"'
    exit 1
}

# --- backend -------------------------------------------------------------
$backendDir = Join-Path $root 'backend'
$jar = Join-Path $backendDir 'target\webox-backend-1.0.0.jar'

if (-not (Test-Path $jar)) {
    Write-Host 'Building the backend (first run downloads dependencies)...'
    Push-Location $backendDir
    if (Test-Path '.\mvnw.cmd') { & .\mvnw.cmd -B -q package -DskipTests }
    else { & mvn -B -q package -DskipTests }
    Pop-Location
}

Write-Host 'Starting the backend on http://localhost:8080 ...'
Start-Process -FilePath (Join-Path $JavaHome 'bin\java.exe') `
    -ArgumentList '-jar', $jar `
    -WorkingDirectory $backendDir `
    -RedirectStandardOutput (Join-Path $backendDir 'backend.log') `
    -RedirectStandardError (Join-Path $backendDir 'backend.err.log')

# --- frontend ------------------------------------------------------------
$frontendDir = Join-Path $root 'frontend'
if (-not (Test-Path (Join-Path $frontendDir 'node_modules'))) {
    Write-Host 'Installing frontend dependencies...'
    Push-Location $frontendDir
    npm install --no-audit --no-fund
    Pop-Location
}

Write-Host 'Starting the SPA on http://localhost:5173 ...'
Start-Process -FilePath 'npm.cmd' -ArgumentList 'run', 'dev' -WorkingDirectory $frontendDir

# --- wait for readiness --------------------------------------------------
$backendReady = $false
for ($i = 1; $i -le 45; $i++) {
    Start-Sleep -Seconds 2
    try {
        Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'http://localhost:8080/actuator/health' -TimeoutSec 4 -UseBasicParsing | Out-Null
        $backendReady = $true
        break
    } catch { }
}

$frontendReady = $false
for ($i = 1; $i -le 30; $i++) {
    Start-Sleep -Seconds 1
    try {
        Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'http://localhost:5173/' -TimeoutSec 3 -UseBasicParsing | Out-Null
        $frontendReady = $true
        break
    } catch { }
}

Write-Host ''
Write-Host ('backend  : ' + $(if ($backendReady) { 'UP  http://localhost:8080' } else { 'NOT RESPONDING - see backend/backend.log' }))
Write-Host ('frontend : ' + $(if ($frontendReady) { 'UP  http://localhost:5173' } else { 'NOT RESPONDING - see the npm window' }))
Write-Host ''
Write-Host 'Employee app : http://localhost:5173'
Write-Host 'Console      : http://localhost:5173/console'
Write-Host 'API docs     : http://localhost:8080/swagger-ui.html'
Write-Host 'Admin login  : admin@webox.com / Admin1234'
","file_path":"D:\G\MyRep\webox\scripts\dev.ps1"}

{"content":"# WeBox · API Reference

Base URL: `http://localhost:8080`
Interactive documentation (Swagger UI): `http://localhost:8080/swagger-ui.html`
OpenAPI JSON: `http://localhost:8080/v3/api-docs`

All endpoints are prefixed with `/api`. Every user-facing message returned by this API is in
**English** (PRD section 1). Money is transmitted as a decimal **string** so that it can be parsed
into integer cents without ever passing through a floating point type.

---

## Conventions

### Authentication

Employee endpoints require a bearer token obtained from `POST /api/auth/register` or
`POST /api/auth/login`:

```
Authorization: Bearer <jwt>
```

The token carries the caller's role. Endpoints under `/api/admin/**` additionally require the
`ADMIN` role; an employee token receives `403 FORBIDDEN`, even if the SPA guard is bypassed.

### Response envelope

Every response - success or failure - uses the same shape:

```json
{
  "code": "OK",
  "message": "Success",
  "data": { },
  "requestId": "8f3c1a2e"
}
```

`requestId` is also returned as the `X-Request-Id` response header and appears in the server log,
so a reported failure can be traced to its log lines.

### Pagination

Paged endpoints return this inside `data`:

```json
{
  "items": [],
  "page": 0,
  "size": 12,
  "total": 50,
  "totalPages": 5
}
```

`size` is capped at 50. `page` is zero-based.

### Money

Amounts are strings with exactly two decimals:

```json
{ "price": "22.50", "totalAmount": "121.50" }
```

### Dates and timestamps

Business dates are `yyyy-MM-dd` (`mealDate`, `menuDate`). Audit timestamps are ISO-8601 UTC.

---

## Error codes

| Code | HTTP | When it happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `VALIDATION_FAILED` | 400 | A field is missing, too long, or malformed. `data.fieldErrors` lists the offending fields. |
| `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED` | 400 | `POST /api/orders` without the `Idempotency-Key` header. |
| `ORDER_SIZE_EXCEEDED` | 400 | More than 5 portions in one order. |
| `OPTION_INVALID` | 400 | A required option group is unanswered, a single-choice group has several selections, an option does not belong to the dish, or it was discontinued. |
| `DISH_NOT_ON_MENU` | 400 | The dish is not on the menu for the resolved meal date. |
| `UPLOAD_INVALID_TYPE` | 400 | An uploaded file is not a real JPG/PNG/WebP (verified by magic bytes). |
| `UPLOAD_TOO_LARGE` | 400 | An uploaded file exceeds 2 MB. |
| `UNAUTHENTICATED` | 401 | Missing, malformed, or expired token. |
| `AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS` | 401 | Wrong email **or** wrong password - deliberately indistinguishable. |
| `FORBIDDEN` | 403 | Insufficient role, or the resource belongs to another employee. |
| `DISH_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Unknown dish, or an off-shelf dish requested by an employee. |
| `ORDER_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Unknown order. |
| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Unknown route or stored image. |
| `EMAIL_ALREADY_REGISTERED` | 409 | The email is taken. |
| `DISH_UNAVAILABLE` | 409 | The dish was taken off the shelf after it was added to the cart. |
| `ORDER_SLOT_CONFLICT` | 409 | An active order already exists for that meal. `data` carries `existingOrderId` and `orderNo`. |
| `ORDER_IN_PROGRESS` | 409 | The same idempotency key is still being processed. Rare: a duplicate submit normally waits and returns the original order. |
| `ORDER_NOT_CANCELLABLE` | 409 | Only `Pending` orders can be cancelled. |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | 500 | Unexpected failure. Contains no stack trace; correlate with `requestId`. |

Example failure:

```json
{
  "code": "ORDER_SLOT_CONFLICT",
  "message": "You already have an active order for this meal. Please view it instead.",
  "data": { "existingOrderId": 42, "orderNo": "WB20260324-000123" },
  "requestId": "8f3c1a2e"
}
```

---

## Authentication

### POST /api/auth/register — public

Creates an employee account and returns a token, so a new user is signed in immediately.

| Field | Type | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `email` | string | required, valid email, ≤ 200 chars, must be unique (stored lower-cased) |
| `password` | string | required, 8–64 chars, must contain both a letter and a digit, no whitespace |
| `displayName` | string | required, ≤ 50 chars |

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/auth/register \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"alex@example.com","password":"Passw0rd123","displayName":"Alex Chen"}'
```

`201 Created`

```json
{
  "code": "OK",
  "message": "Success",
  "data": {
    "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9...",
    "tokenType": "Bearer",
    "expiresInSeconds": 28800,
    "user": { "id": 3, "email": "alex@example.com", "displayName": "Alex Chen", "role": "EMPLOYEE" }
  },
  "requestId": "a1b2c3d4"
}
```

### POST /api/auth/login — public

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/auth/login \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"admin@webox.com","password":"Admin1234"}'
```

Same response shape as register. `200 OK`.

### GET /api/auth/me — authenticated

Returns the current user. The SPA calls this on cold start so a page refresh keeps the session.

```json
{ "id": 3, "email": "alex@example.com", "displayName": "Alex Chen", "role": "EMPLOYEE" }
```

---

## Menu

### GET /api/menu — authenticated

The daily menu, filtered, optionally re-ordered by preference, and paged.

| Query parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `date` | date | today | Menu date. |
| `categories` | string, repeatable | all | `?categories=Chinese&categories=Japanese` selects the union. |
| `keyword` | string | — | ≤ 50 chars; matched against **name and description**, case-insensitively. |
| `page` | int | 0 | |
| `size` | int | 12 | 1–50 |
| `prefer` | bool | false | Applies the caller's preferred cuisines and spice level to ordering and highlighting. |

```bash
curl 'http://localhost:8080/api/menu?date=2026-03-24&categories=Chinese&categories=Japanese&size=2' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

```json
{
  "code": "OK",
  "message": "Success",
  "data": {
    "items": [
      {
        "dishId": 1,
        "name": "Kung Pao Chicken",
        "description": "Classic Sichuan dish, chicken stir-fried with peanuts and dried chili",
        "price": "22.00",
        "category": "Chinese",
        "spiceLevel": "Medium",
        "imageUrl": "/dishes/dish-01.jpg",
        "proteins": ["Chicken"],
        "allergens": ["Peanuts"],
        "dailyQty": 50,
        "remainingQty": 50,
        "hasOptions": false,
        "recommended": false,
        "matchTags": []
      }
    ],
    "page": 0,
    "size": 2,
    "total": 12,
    "totalPages": 6
  },
  "requestId": "3f9a11c2"
}
```

`hasOptions` tells the SPA whether "Add to Cart" can add directly or must open the detail page to
collect the required choices. `remainingQty` is populated from the daily menu row; the deduction
that makes it move is a Tier 3 extension point.

With `prefer=true` and configured preferences, matching dishes come first and carry
`recommended: true` plus `matchTags` such as `["Preferred cuisine","Matches your spice level"]`.

### GET /api/menu/dates — authenticated

Dates between today and today + 7 that have a published menu, ascending.

```json
["2026-03-24", "2026-03-25"]
```

### GET /api/menu/dishes/{id} — authenticated

Full detail: description, proteins, allergens, spice level, and the customization groups.

| Query parameter | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `date` | date | Used to report that date's `dailyQty` / `remainingQty`. Defaults to today. |

```json
{
  "dishId": 9,
  "name": "Classic Beef Burger",
  "description": "Angus beef patty with lettuce, tomato, onion",
  "price": "38.00",
  "category": "Western",
  "spiceLevel": "None",
  "imageUrl": "/dishes/dish-09.jpg",
  "proteins": ["Beef"],
  "allergens": ["Gluten", "Dairy"],
  "available": true,
  "dailyQty": 50,
  "remainingQty": 50,
  "optionGroups": [
    {
      "groupId": 12,
      "name": "Bun",
      "required": true,
      "selectionType": "SINGLE",
      "options": [
        { "optionId": 31, "name": "Plain", "priceDelta": "0.00", "available": true },
        { "optionId": 32, "name": "Whole Wheat", "priceDelta": "0.00", "available": true }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Requesting an off-shelf dish returns `404 DISH_NOT_FOUND`, because employees cannot see it.

---

## Preferences

### GET /api/users/me/preferences — authenticated

```json
{
  "allergens": ["Peanuts", "Egg"],
  "preferredCategories": ["Japanese", "Light Meal"],
  "spicePreference": "Mild",
  "tastePreference": "Light",
  "budgetMin": "15.00",
  "budgetMax": "30.00",
  "configured": true
}
```

All enum values travel as their English labels. `configured` is false when nothing has been saved.

### PUT /api/users/me/preferences — authenticated

Replaces the whole object, so the call is idempotent. All fields are optional.

```bash
curl -X PUT http://localhost:8080/api/users/me/preferences \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
        "allergens": ["Peanuts"],
        "preferredCategories": ["Japanese"],
        "spicePreference": "Mild",
        "tastePreference": "Light",
        "budgetMin": "15.00",
        "budgetMax": "30.00"
      }'
```

Returns `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` when `budgetMin > budgetMax`.

**Semantics worth noting**: allergens produce a warning when a matching dish is added to the cart -
they never hide a dish. `tastePreference` is stored for recommendations and never reorders the menu.

### GET /api/users/me/addresses — authenticated

Delivery addresses used previously, most recent first. The checkout page offers these and
remembers any new address after a successful order.

```json
[ { "id": 5, "addressText": "Building A, Desk 101", "useCount": 3, "lastUsedAt": "2026-03-24T02:10:11Z" } ]
```

---

## Orders

### POST /api/orders/checkout-preview — authenticated

Prices and validates the cart before anything is created, so problems surface on page entry
rather than after pressing "Place Order". It accepts **only** what it needs; the delivery address
is not part of this contract.

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/orders/checkout-preview \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
        "items": [{ "lineKey": "9#31-40", "dishId": 9, "quantity": 2, "optionIds": [31, 40] }],
        "deliveryDate": "2026-03-24",
        "mealSlot": "Lunch"
      }'
```

```json
{
  "bookableDates": ["2026-03-24", "2026-03-25"],
  "resolved": {
    "mealDate": "2026-03-24",
    "mealSlot": "Dinner",
    "adjusted": true,
    "reasonCode": "LUNCH_CUTOFF_PASSED"
  },
  "pricedItems": [
    {
      "lineKey": "9#31-40",
      "dishId": 9,
      "name": "Classic Beef Burger",
      "unitPrice": "43.00",
      "quantity": 2,
      "subtotal": "86.00",
      "optionLabels": ["Plain", "Mustard"]
    }
  ],
  "total": "86.00",
  "unavailableItems": [],
  "existingOrder": null,
  "budget": { "min": "15.00", "max": "30.00", "cartTotal": "86.00", "exceedsMax": true }
}
```

* `resolved.adjusted = true` means the cut-off rules moved the meal. `reasonCode` is
  `LUNCH_CUTOFF_PASSED` or `DINNER_CUTOFF_PASSED`.
* `unavailableItems[].reason` is one of `DISH_NOT_FOUND`, `DISH_UNAVAILABLE`, `DISH_NOT_ON_MENU`,
  `OPTION_INVALID`.
* `existingOrder` being non-null is the signal to render **"View Existing Order"** instead of
  "Place Order" (PRD 4.2).
* `budget.exceedsMax` drives a non-blocking warning; ordering is never blocked by budget.

### POST /api/orders — authenticated

Places an order. **The `Idempotency-Key` header is mandatory.** Generate it once when the checkout
page mounts and reuse it for every retry of that submission.

| Header | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `Idempotency-Key` | client-generated UUID, ≤ 64 chars |

| Body field | Type | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items[].lineKey` | string | optional, ≤ 120 chars, echoed back so the client can match rows |
| `items[].dishId` | long | required |
| `items[].quantity` | int | 1–5 per line; the **sum** across lines must be ≤ 5 |
| `items[].optionIds` | long[] | chosen option ids; validated against the dish |
| `deliveryDate` | date | required; today … today + 7 |
| `mealSlot` | `Lunch` \| `Dinner` | required |
| `deliveryAddress` | string | required, ≤ 200 chars |
| `note` | string | optional, ≤ 200 chars |

The server ignores any price the client sends and recomputes everything from the database.

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/orders \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
        "items": [{ "lineKey": "9#31-40", "dishId": 9, "quantity": 2, "optionIds": [31, 40] }],
        "deliveryDate": "2026-03-24",
        "mealSlot": "Lunch",
        "deliveryAddress": "Building A, Desk 101",
        "note": "No cutlery please"
      }'
```

```json
{
  "id": 42,
  "orderNo": "WB20260324-000123",
  "status": "Pending",
  "mealDate": "2026-03-24",
  "mealSlot": "Dinner",
  "requestedMealSlot": "Lunch",
  "slotAdjusted": true,
  "deliveryAddress": "Building A, Desk 101",
  "note": "No cutlery please",
  "itemCount": 2,
  "totalAmount": "86.00",
  "createdAt": "2026-03-24T02:10:11.123Z",
  "cancelledAt": null,
  "duplicated": false,
  "items": [
    {
      "id": 77,
      "dishId": 9,
      "dishName": "Classic Beef Burger",
      "imageUrl": "/dishes/dish-09.jpg",
      "unitBasePrice": "38.00",
      "unitPrice": "43.00",
      "quantity": 2,
      "subtotal": "86.00",
      "options": [
        { "groupName": "Bun", "optionName": "Plain", "priceDelta": "0.00" },
        { "groupName": "Sauce", "optionName": "Mustard", "priceDelta": "0.00" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

`duplicated: true` marks a response that replayed an existing order instead of creating one. The
same is true of the order lines: they are immutable snapshots, so later edits to the dish never
change a historical order.

**Guarantees**

* Submitting the same key concurrently 10 times creates exactly one order; all 10 responses carry
  the same `orderNo`, and 9 of them report `duplicated: true`.
* At most one `Pending`/`Confirmed` order exists per employee per meal. A racing request receives
  `409 ORDER_SLOT_CONFLICT` with the existing order in `data`.
* Both guarantees are enforced by unique indexes in MySQL, so they hold even if Redis is down or
  several application instances run in parallel.

### GET /api/orders — authenticated

My orders, newest first. `page` (default 0) and `size` (default 10, max 50).

### GET /api/orders/{id} — authenticated (owner only)

Full order detail including the option snapshot. Another employee's order returns
`403 FORBIDDEN`.

### POST /api/orders/{id}/cancel — authenticated (owner only)

Cancels a `Pending` order and releases its meal slot immediately.

* `Pending` → cancelled, `200`.
* Already `Cancelled` → `200` with the current state (idempotent).
* `Confirmed` or `Completed` → `409 ORDER_NOT_CANCELLABLE`.

---

## Console (ADMIN role required)

### GET /api/admin/dishes

| Query parameter | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `keyword` | string | ≤ 50 chars, matched against the dish name |
| `category` | string | one of the six cuisine labels |
| `available` | bool | shelf-status filter |
| `page`, `size` | int | default 0 / 10, max 50 |

Returns the same paged envelope, with each dish carrying its full option graph.

### GET /api/admin/dishes/{id}

A single dish, including option groups and options.

### POST /api/admin/dishes — `201 Created`

### PUT /api/admin/dishes/{id}

Both take the same body. `optionGroups` **replaces** the dish's option graph in one transaction.
Orders already placed are unaffected because their lines are snapshots.

```json
{
  "name": "Smoke Test Bowl",
  "description": "Dish created by the automated test",
  "price": "19.90",
  "category": "Light Meal",
  "spiceLevel": "Mild",
  "imageUrl": "/api/files/images/6f1c...e2.jpg",
  "allergens": ["Soy"],
  "proteins": ["Tofu"],
  "available": true,

that stay on the menu are updated in place, which preserves `soldQty` if today's menu is edited
mid-service.

schedules tomorrow and adjusts today.

{"content":"# WeBox · API Reference

Base URL: `http://localhost:8080`
Interactive documentation (Swagger UI): `http://localhost:8080/swagger-ui.html`
OpenAPI JSON: `http://localhost:8080/v3/api-docs`

All endpoints are prefixed with `/api`. Every user-facing message returned by this API is in
**English** (PRD section 1). Money is transmitted as a decimal **string** so that it can be parsed
into integer cents without ever passing through a floating point type.

---

## Conventions

### Authentication

Employee endpoints require a bearer token obtained from `POST /api/auth/register` or
`POST /api/auth/login`:

```
Authorization: Bearer <jwt>
```

The token carries the caller's role. Endpoints under `/api/admin/**` additionally require the
`ADMIN` role; an employee token receives `403 FORBIDDEN`, even if the SPA guard is bypassed.

### Response envelope

Every response - success or failure - uses the same shape:

```json
{
  "code": "OK",
  "message": "Success",
  "data": { },
  "requestId": "8f3c1a2e"
}
```

`requestId` is also returned as the `X-Request-Id` response header and appears in the server log,
so a reported failure can be traced to its log lines.

### Pagination

Paged endpoints return this inside `data`:

```json
{
  "items": [],
  "page": 0,
  "size": 12,
  "total": 50,
  "totalPages": 5
}
```

`size` is capped at 50. `page` is zero-based.

### Money

Amounts are strings with exactly two decimals:

```json
{ "price": "22.50", "totalAmount": "121.50" }
```

### Dates and timestamps

Business dates are `yyyy-MM-dd` (`mealDate`, `menuDate`). Audit timestamps are ISO-8601 UTC.

---

## Error codes

| Code | HTTP | When it happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `VALIDATION_FAILED` | 400 | A field is missing, too long, or malformed. `data.fieldErrors` lists the offending fields. |
| `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED` | 400 | `POST /api/orders` without the `Idempotency-Key` header. |
| `ORDER_SIZE_EXCEEDED` | 400 | More than 5 portions in one order. |
| `OPTION_INVALID` | 400 | A required option group is unanswered, a single-choice group has several selections, an option does not belong to the dish, or it was discontinued. |
| `DISH_NOT_ON_MENU` | 400 | The dish is not on the menu for the resolved meal date. |
| `UPLOAD_INVALID_TYPE` | 400 | An uploaded file is not a real JPG/PNG/WebP (verified by magic bytes). |
| `UPLOAD_TOO_LARGE` | 400 | An uploaded file exceeds 2 MB. |
| `UNAUTHENTICATED` | 401 | Missing, malformed, or expired token. |
| `AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS` | 401 | Wrong email **or** wrong password - deliberately indistinguishable. |
| `FORBIDDEN` | 403 | Insufficient role, or the resource belongs to another employee. |
| `DISH_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Unknown dish, or an off-shelf dish requested by an employee. |
| `ORDER_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Unknown order. |
| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Unknown route or stored image. |
| `EMAIL_ALREADY_REGISTERED` | 409 | The email is taken. |
| `DISH_UNAVAILABLE` | 409 | The dish was taken off the shelf after it was added to the cart. |
| `ORDER_SLOT_CONFLICT` | 409 | An active order already exists for that meal. `data` carries `existingOrderId` and `orderNo`. |
| `ORDER_IN_PROGRESS` | 409 | The same idempotency key is still being processed. Rare: a duplicate submit normally waits and returns the original order. |
| `ORDER_NOT_CANCELLABLE` | 409 | Only `Pending` orders can be cancelled. |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | 500 | Unexpected failure. Contains no stack trace; correlate with `requestId`. |

Example failure:

```json
{
  "code": "ORDER_SLOT_CONFLICT",
  "message": "You already have an active order for this meal. Please view it instead.",
  "data": { "existingOrderId": 42, "orderNo": "WB20260324-000123" },
  "requestId": "8f3c1a2e"
}
```

---

## Authentication

### POST /api/auth/register — public

Creates an employee account and returns a token, so a new user is signed in immediately.

| Field | Type | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `email` | string | required, valid email, ≤ 200 chars, must be unique (stored lower-cased) |
| `password` | string | required, 8–64 chars, must contain both a letter and a digit, no whitespace |
| `displayName` | string | required, ≤ 50 chars |

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/auth/register \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"alex@example.com","password":"Passw0rd123","displayName":"Alex Chen"}'
```

`201 Created`

```json
{
  "code": "OK",
  "message": "Success",
  "data": {
    "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9...",
    "tokenType": "Bearer",
    "expiresInSeconds": 28800,
    "user": { "id": 3, "email": "alex@example.com", "displayName": "Alex Chen", "role": "EMPLOYEE" }
  },
  "requestId": "a1b2c3d4"
}
```

### POST /api/auth/login — public

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/auth/login \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"admin@webox.com","password":"Admin1234"}'
```

Same response shape as register. `200 OK`.

### GET /api/auth/me — authenticated

Returns the current user. The SPA calls this on cold start so a page refresh keeps the session.

```json
{ "id": 3, "email": "alex@example.com", "displayName": "Alex Chen", "role": "EMPLOYEE" }
```

---

## Menu

### GET /api/menu — authenticated

The daily menu, filtered, optionally re-ordered by preference, and paged.

| Query parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `date` | date | today | Menu date. |
| `categories` | string, repeatable | all | `?categories=Chinese&categories=Japanese` selects the union. |
| `keyword` | string | — | ≤ 50 chars; matched against **name and description**, case-insensitively. |
| `page` | int | 0 | |
| `size` | int | 12 | 1–50 |
| `prefer` | bool | false | Applies the caller's preferred cuisines and spice level to ordering and highlighting. |

```bash
curl 'http://localhost:8080/api/menu?date=2026-03-24&categories=Chinese&categories=Japanese&size=2' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

```json
{
  "code": "OK",
  "message": "Success",
  "data": {
    "items": [
      {
        "dishId": 1,
        "name": "Kung Pao Chicken",
        "description": "Classic Sichuan dish, chicken stir-fried with peanuts and dried chili",
        "price": "22.00",
        "category": "Chinese",
        "spiceLevel": "Medium",
        "imageUrl": "/dishes/dish-01.jpg",
        "proteins": ["Chicken"],
        "allergens": ["Peanuts"],
        "dailyQty": 50,
        "remainingQty": 50,
        "hasOptions": false,
        "recommended": false,
        "matchTags": []
      }
    ],
    "page": 0,
    "size": 2,
    "total": 12,
    "totalPages": 6
  },
  "requestId": "3f9a11c2"
}
```

`hasOptions` tells the SPA whether "Add to Cart" can add directly or must open the detail page to
collect the required choices. `remainingQty` is populated from the daily menu row; the deduction
that makes it move is a Tier 3 extension point.

`recommended: true` plus `matchTags` such as `["Preferred cuisine","Matches your spice level"]`.

| Query parameter | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `date` | date | Used to report that date's `dailyQty` / `remainingQty`. Defaults to today. |

```json

  "remainingQty": 50,
  "optionGroups": [
    {
      "groupId": 12,
      "name": "Bun",
      "required": true,
      "selectionType": "SINGLE",
      "options": [
        { "optionId": 31, "name": "Plain", "priceDelta": "0.00", "available": true },

```

## Preferences

### GET /api/users/me/preferences — authenticated

```json
{
  "allergens": ["Peanuts", "Egg"],
  "preferredCategories": ["Japanese", "Light Meal"],
  "spicePreference": "Mild",
  "tastePreference": "Light",
  "budgetMin": "15.00",
  "budgetMax": "30.00",
  "configured": true
}
```

All enum values travel as their English labels. `configured` is false when nothing has been saved.

### PUT /api/users/me/preferences — authenticated

Replaces the whole object, so the call is idempotent. All fields are optional.

```bash
curl -X PUT http://localhost:8080/api/users/me/preferences \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
        "allergens": ["Peanuts"],
        "preferredCategories": ["Japanese"],
        "spicePreference": "Mild",
        "tastePreference": "Light",
        "budgetMin": "15.00",
        "budgetMax": "30.00"
      }'
```

Returns `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` when `budgetMin > budgetMax`.

**Semantics worth noting**: allergens produce a warning when a matching dish is added to the cart -
they never hide a dish. `tastePreference` is stored for recommendations and never reorders the menu.

### GET /api/users/me/addresses — authenticated

Delivery addresses used previously, most recent first. The checkout page offers these and
remembers any new address after a successful order.

## Orders

### POST /api/orders/checkout-preview — authenticated

Prices and validates the cart before anything is created, so problems surface on page entry
rather than after pressing "Place Order". It accepts **only** what it needs; the delivery address
is not part of this contract.

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/orders/checkout-preview \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
        "items": [{ "lineKey": "9#31-40", "dishId": 9, "quantity": 2, "optionIds": [31, 40] }],
        "deliveryDate": "2026-03-24",
        "mealSlot": "Lunch"
      }'
```

```json
{
  "bookableDates": ["2026-03-24", "2026-03-25"],
  "resolved": {
    "mealDate": "2026-03-24",
    "mealSlot": "Dinner",
    "adjusted": true,
    "reasonCode": "LUNCH_CUTOFF_PASSED"
  },
  "pricedItems": [
    {
      "lineKey": "9#31-40",
      "dishId": 9,
      "name": "Classic Beef Burger",
      "unitPrice": "43.00",
      "quantity": 2,
      "subtotal": "86.00",
      "optionLabels": ["Plain", "Mustard"]
    }
  ],
  "total": "86.00",
  "unavailableItems": [],
  "existingOrder": null,
  "budget": { "min": "15.00", "max": "30.00", "cartTotal": "86.00", "exceedsMax": true }
}
```

* `resolved.adjusted = true` means the cut-off rules moved the meal. `reasonCode` is
  `LUNCH_CUTOFF_PASSED` or `DINNER_CUTOFF_PASSED`.
* `unavailableItems[].reason` is one of `DISH_NOT_FOUND`, `DISH_UNAVAILABLE`, `DISH_NOT_ON_MENU`,
  `OPTION_INVALID`.
* `existingOrder` being non-null is the signal to render **"View Existing Order"** instead of
  "Place Order" (PRD 4.2).
* `budget.exceedsMax` drives a non-blocking warning; ordering is never blocked by budget.

### POST /api/orders — authenticated

Places an order. **The `Idempotency-Key` header is mandatory.** Generate it once when the checkout
page mounts and reuse it for every retry of that submission.

| Header | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `Idempotency-Key` | client-generated UUID, ≤ 64 chars |

| Body field | Type | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items[].lineKey` | string | optional, ≤ 120 chars, echoed back so the client can match rows |
| `items[].dishId` | long | required |
| `items[].quantity` | int | 1–5 per line; the **sum** across lines must be ≤ 5 |
| `items[].optionIds` | long[] | chosen option ids; validated against the dish |
| `deliveryDate` | date | required; today … today + 7 |
| `mealSlot` | `Lunch` \| `Dinner` | required |
| `deliveryAddress` | string | required, ≤ 200 chars |
| `note` | string | optional, ≤ 200 chars |

The server ignores any price the client sends and recomputes everything from the database.

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/orders \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
        "items": [{ "lineKey": "9#31-40", "dishId": 9, "quantity": 2, "optionIds": [31, 40] }],
        "deliveryDate": "2026-03-24",
        "mealSlot": "Lunch",
        "deliveryAddress": "Building A, Desk 101",
        "note": "No cutlery please"
      }'
```

```json
{
  "id": 42,
  "orderNo": "WB20260324-000123",
  "status": "Pending",
  "mealDate": "2026-03-24",
  "mealSlot": "Dinner",
  "requestedMealSlot": "Lunch",
  "slotAdjusted": true,
  "deliveryAddress": "Building A, Desk 101",
  "note": "No cutlery please",
  "itemCount": 2,
  "totalAmount": "86.00",
  "createdAt": "2026-03-24T02:10:11.123Z",
  "cancelledAt": null,
  "duplicated": false,
  "items": [
    {
      "id": 77,
      "dishId": 9,
      "dishName": "Classic Beef Burger",
      "imageUrl": "/dishes/dish-09.jpg",
      "unitBasePrice": "38.00",
      "unitPrice": "43.00",
      "quantity": 2,
      "subtotal": "86.00",
      "options": [
        { "groupName": "Bun", "optionName": "Plain", "priceDelta": "0.00" },
        { "groupName": "Sauce", "optionName": "Mustard", "priceDelta": "0.00" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

`duplicated: true` marks a response that replayed an existing order instead of creating one. The
same is true of the order lines: they are immutable snapshots, so later edits to the dish never
change a historical order.

**Guarantees**

* Submitting the same key concurrently 10 times creates exactly one order; all 10 responses carry
  the same `orderNo`, and 9 of them report `duplicated: true`.
* At most one `Pending`/`Confirmed` order exists per employee per meal. A racing request receives
  `409 ORDER_SLOT_CONFLICT` with the existing order in `data`.
* Both guarantees are enforced by unique indexes in MySQL, so they hold even if Redis is down or
  several application instances run in parallel.

### GET /api/orders — authenticated

My orders, newest first. `page` (default 0) and `size` (default 10, max 50).

### GET /api/orders/{id} — authenticated (owner only)

Full order detail including the option snapshot. Another employee's order returns
`403 FORBIDDEN`.

### POST /api/orders/{id}/cancel — authenticated (owner only)

Cancels a `Pending` order and releases its meal slot immediately.

* `Pending` → cancelled, `200`.
* Already `Cancelled` → `200` with the current state (idempotent).
* `Confirmed` or `Completed` → `409 ORDER_NOT_CANCELLABLE`.

{"content":"# WeBox · API Reference

Base URL: `http://localhost:8080`
Interactive documentation (Swagger UI): `http://localhost:8080/swagger-ui.html`
OpenAPI JSON: `http://localhost:8080/v3/api-docs`

All endpoints are prefixed with `/api`. Every user-facing message returned by this API is in
**English** (PRD section 1). Money is transmitted as a decimal **string** so that it can be parsed
into integer cents without ever passing through a floating point type.

---

## Conventions

### Authentication

Employee endpoints require a bearer token obtained from `POST /api/auth/register` or
`POST /api/auth/login`:

```
Authorization: Bearer <jwt>
```

The token carries the caller's role. Endpoints under `/api/admin/**` additionally require the
`ADMIN` role; an employee token receives `403 FORBIDDEN`, even if the SPA guard is bypassed.

### Response envelope

Every response - success or failure - uses the same shape:

```json
{
  "code": "OK",
  "message": "Success",
  "data": { },
  "requestId": "8f3c1a2e"
}
```

`requestId` is also returned as the `X-Request-Id` response header and appears in the server log,
so a reported failure can be traced to its log lines.

### Pagination

Paged endpoints return this inside `data`:

```json
{
  "items": [],
  "page": 0,
  "size": 12,
  "total": 50,
  "totalPages": 5
}
```

`size` is capped at 50. `page` is zero-based.

### Money

Amounts are strings with exactly two decimals:

```json
{ "price": "22.50", "totalAmount": "121.50" }
```

### Dates and timestamps

Business dates are `yyyy-MM-dd` (`mealDate`, `menuDate`). Audit timestamps are ISO-8601 UTC.

---

## Error codes

| Code | HTTP | When it happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `VALIDATION_FAILED` | 400 | A field is missing, too long, or malformed. `data.fieldErrors` lists the offending fields. |
| `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED` | 400 | `POST /api/orders` without the `Idempotency-Key` header. |
| `ORDER_SIZE_EXCEEDED` | 400 | More than 5 portions in one order. |
| `OPTION_INVALID` | 400 | A required option group is unanswered, a single-choice group has several selections, an option does not belong to the dish, or it was discontinued. |
| `DISH_NOT_ON_MENU` | 400 | The dish is not on the menu for the resolved meal date. |
| `UPLOAD_INVALID_TYPE` | 400 | An uploaded file is not a real JPG/PNG/WebP (verified by magic bytes). |
| `UPLOAD_TOO_LARGE` | 400 | An uploaded file exceeds 2 MB. |
| `UNAUTHENTICATED` | 401 | Missing, malformed, or expired token. |
| `AUTH_INVALID_CREDENTIALS` | 401 | Wrong email **or** wrong password - deliberately indistinguishable. |
| `FORBIDDEN` | 403 | Insufficient role, or the resource belongs to another employee. |
| `DISH_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Unknown dish, or an off-shelf dish requested by an employee. |
| `ORDER_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Unknown order. |
| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Unknown route or stored image. |
| `EMAIL_ALREADY_REGISTERED` | 409 | The email is taken. |
| `DISH_UNAVAILABLE` | 409 | The dish was taken off the shelf after it was added to the cart. |
| `ORDER_SLOT_CONFLICT` | 409 | An active order already exists for that meal. `data` carries `existingOrderId` and `orderNo`. |
| `ORDER_IN_PROGRESS` | 409 | The same idempotency key is still being processed. Rare: a duplicate submit normally waits and returns the original order. |
| `ORDER_NOT_CANCELLABLE` | 409 | Only `Pending` orders can be cancelled. |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | 500 | Unexpected failure. Contains no stack trace; correlate with `requestId`. |

Example failure:

```json
{
  "code": "ORDER_SLOT_CONFLICT",
  "message": "You already have an active order for this meal. Please view it instead.",
  "data": { "existingOrderId": 42, "orderNo": "WB20260324-000123" },
  "requestId": "8f3c1a2e"
}
```

---

## Authentication

### POST /api/auth/register — public

Creates an employee account and returns a token, so a new user is signed in immediately.

| Field | Type | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `email` | string | required, valid email, ≤ 200 chars, must be unique (stored lower-cased) |
| `password` | string | required, 8–64 chars, must contain both a letter and a digit, no whitespace |
| `displayName` | string | required, ≤ 50 chars |

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/auth/register \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"alex@example.com","password":"Passw0rd123","displayName":"Alex Chen"}'
```

`201 Created`

```json
{
  "code": "OK",
  "message": "Success",
  "data": {
    "token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9...",
    "tokenType": "Bearer",
    "expiresInSeconds": 28800,
    "user": { "id": 3, "email": "alex@example.com", "displayName": "Alex Chen", "role": "EMPLOYEE" }
  },
  "requestId": "a1b2c3d4"
}
```

### POST /api/auth/login — public

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/auth/login \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"admin@webox.com","password":"Admin1234"}'
```

Same response shape as register. `200 OK`.

### GET /api/auth/me — authenticated

Returns the current user. The SPA calls this on cold start so a page refresh keeps the session.

```json
{ "id": 3, "email": "alex@example.com", "displayName": "Alex Chen", "role": "EMPLOYEE" }
```

---

## Menu

### GET /api/menu — authenticated

The daily menu, filtered, optionally re-ordered by preference, and paged.

| Query parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `date` | date | today | Menu date. |
| `categories` | string, repeatable | all | `?categories=Chinese&categories=Japanese` selects the union. |
| `keyword` | string | — | ≤ 50 chars; matched against **name and description**, case-insensitively. |
| `page` | int | 0 | |
| `size` | int | 12 | 1–50 |
| `prefer` | bool | false | Applies the caller's preferred cuisines and spice level to ordering and highlighting. |

```bash
curl 'http://localhost:8080/api/menu?date=2026-03-24&categories=Chinese&categories=Japanese&size=2' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

```json
{
  "code": "OK",
  "message": "Success",
  "data": {
    "items": [
      {
        "dishId": 1,
        "name": "Kung Pao Chicken",
        "description": "Classic Sichuan dish, chicken stir-fried with peanuts and dried chili",
        "price": "22.00",
        "category": "Chinese",
        "spiceLevel": "Medium",
        "imageUrl": "/dishes/dish-01.jpg",
        "proteins": ["Chicken"],
        "allergens": ["Peanuts"],
        "dailyQty": 50,
        "remainingQty": 50,
        "hasOptions": false,
        "recommended": false,
        "matchTags": []
      }
    ],
    "page": 0,
    "size": 2,
    "total": 12,
    "totalPages": 6
  },
  "requestId": "3f9a11c2"
}
```

`hasOptions` tells the SPA whether "Add to Cart" can add directly or must open the detail page to
collect the required choices. `remainingQty` is populated from the daily menu row; the deduction
that makes it move is a Tier 3 extension point.

With `prefer=true` and configured preferences, matching dishes come first and carry
`recommended: true` plus `matchTags` such as `["Preferred cuisine","Matches your spice level"]`.

### GET /api/menu/dates — authenticated

Dates between today and today + 7 that have a published menu, ascending.

```json
["2026-03-24", "2026-03-25"]
```

### GET /api/menu/dishes/{id} — authenticated

Full detail: description, proteins, allergens, spice level, and the customization groups.

| Query parameter | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `date` | date | Used to report that date's `dailyQty` / `remainingQty`. Defaults to today. |

```json
{
  "dishId": 9,
  "name": "Classic Beef Burger",
  "description": "Angus beef patty with lettuce, tomato, onion",
  "price": "38.00",
  "category": "Western",
  "spiceLevel": "None",
  "imageUrl": "/dishes/dish-09.jpg",
  "proteins": ["Beef"],
  "allergens": ["Gluten", "Dairy"],
  "available": true,
  "dailyQty": 50,
  "remainingQty": 50,
  "optionGroups": [
    {
      "groupId": 12,
      "name": "Bun",
      "required": true,
      "selectionType": "SINGLE",
      "options": [
        { "optionId": 31, "name": "Plain", "priceDelta": "0.00", "available": true },
        { "optionId": 32, "name": "Whole Wheat", "priceDelta": "0.00", "available": true }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

Requesting an off-shelf dish returns `404 DISH_NOT_FOUND`, because employees cannot see it.

---

## Preferences

### GET /api/users/me/preferences — authenticated

```json
{
  "allergens": ["Peanuts", "Egg"],
  "preferredCategories": ["Japanese", "Light Meal"],
  "spicePreference": "Mild",
  "tastePreference": "Light",
  "budgetMin": "15.00",
  "budgetMax": "30.00",
  "configured": true
}
```

All enum values travel as their English labels. `configured` is false when nothing has been saved.

### PUT /api/users/me/preferences — authenticated

Replaces the whole object, so the call is idempotent. All fields are optional.

```bash
curl -X PUT http://localhost:8080/api/users/me/preferences \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
        "allergens": ["Peanuts"],
        "preferredCategories": ["Japanese"],
        "spicePreference": "Mild",
        "tastePreference": "Light",
        "budgetMin": "15.00",
        "budgetMax": "30.00"
      }'
```

Returns `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` when `budgetMin > budgetMax`.

**Semantics worth noting**: allergens produce a warning when a matching dish is added to the cart -
they never hide a dish. `tastePreference` is stored for recommendations and never reorders the menu.

### GET /api/users/me/addresses — authenticated

Delivery addresses used previously, most recent first. The checkout page offers these and
remembers any new address after a successful order.

```json
[ { "id": 5, "addressText": "Building A, Desk 101", "useCount": 3, "lastUsedAt": "2026-03-24T02:10:11Z" } ]
```

---

## Orders

### POST /api/orders/checkout-preview — authenticated

Prices and validates the cart before anything is created, so problems surface on page entry
rather than after pressing "Place Order". It accepts **only** what it needs; the delivery address
is not part of this contract.

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/orders/checkout-preview \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
        "items": [{ "lineKey": "9#31-40", "dishId": 9, "quantity": 2, "optionIds": [31, 40] }],
        "deliveryDate": "2026-03-24",
        "mealSlot": "Lunch"
      }'
```

```json
{
  "bookableDates": ["2026-03-24", "2026-03-25"],
  "resolved": {
    "mealDate": "2026-03-24",
    "mealSlot": "Dinner",
    "adjusted": true,
    "reasonCode": "LUNCH_CUTOFF_PASSED"
  },
  "pricedItems": [
    {
      "lineKey": "9#31-40",
      "dishId": 9,
      "name": "Classic Beef Burger",
      "unitPrice": "43.00",
      "quantity": 2,
      "subtotal": "86.00",
      "optionLabels": ["Plain", "Mustard"]
    }
  ],
  "total": "86.00",
  "unavailableItems": [],
  "existingOrder": null,
  "budget": { "min": "15.00", "max": "30.00", "cartTotal": "86.00", "exceedsMax": true }
}
```

* `resolved.adjusted = true` means the cut-off rules moved the meal. `reasonCode` is
  `LUNCH_CUTOFF_PASSED` or `DINNER_CUTOFF_PASSED`.
* `unavailableItems[].reason` is one of `DISH_NOT_FOUND`, `DISH_UNAVAILABLE`, `DISH_NOT_ON_MENU`,
  `OPTION_INVALID`.
* `existingOrder` being non-null is the signal to render **"View Existing Order"** instead of
  "Place Order" (PRD 4.2).
* `budget.exceedsMax` drives a non-blocking warning; ordering is never blocked by budget.

### POST /api/orders — authenticated

Places an order. **The `Idempotency-Key` header is mandatory.** Generate it once when the checkout
page mounts and reuse it for every retry of that submission.

| Header | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `Idempotency-Key` | client-generated UUID, ≤ 64 chars |

| Body field | Type | Rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items[].lineKey` | string | optional, ≤ 120 chars, echoed back so the client can match rows |
| `items[].dishId` | long | required |
| `items[].quantity` | int | 1–5 per line; the **sum** across lines must be ≤ 5 |
| `items[].optionIds` | long[] | chosen option ids; validated against the dish |
| `deliveryDate` | date | required; today … today + 7 |
| `mealSlot` | `Lunch` \| `Dinner` | required |
| `deliveryAddress` | string | required, ≤ 200 chars |
| `note` | string | optional, ≤ 200 chars |

The server ignores any price the client sends and recomputes everything from the database.

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/orders \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
        "items": [{ "lineKey": "9#31-40", "dishId": 9, "quantity": 2, "optionIds": [31, 40] }],
        "deliveryDate": "2026-03-24",
        "mealSlot": "Lunch",
        "deliveryAddress": "Building A, Desk 101",
        "note": "No cutlery please"
      }'
```

```json
{
  "id": 42,
  "orderNo": "WB20260324-000123",
  "status": "Pending",
  "mealDate": "2026-03-24",
  "mealSlot": "Dinner",
  "requestedMealSlot": "Lunch",
  "slotAdjusted": true,
  "deliveryAddress": "Building A, Desk 101",
  "note": "No cutlery please",
  "itemCount": 2,
  "totalAmount": "86.00",
  "createdAt": "2026-03-24T02:10:11.123Z",
  "cancelledAt": null,
  "duplicated": false,
  "items": [
    {
      "id": 77,
      "dishId": 9,
      "dishName": "Classic Beef Burger",
      "imageUrl": "/dishes/dish-09.jpg",
      "unitBasePrice": "38.00",
      "unitPrice": "43.00",
      "quantity": 2,
      "subtotal": "86.00",
      "options": [
        { "groupName": "Bun", "optionName": "Plain", "priceDelta": "0.00" },
        { "groupName": "Sauce", "optionName": "Mustard", "priceDelta": "0.00" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

`duplicated: true` marks a response that replayed an existing order instead of creating one. The
same is true of the order lines: they are immutable snapshots, so later edits to the dish never
change a historical order.

**Guarantees**

* Submitting the same key concurrently 10 times creates exactly one order; all 10 responses carry
  the same `orderNo`, and 9 of them report `duplicated: true`.
* At most one `Pending`/`Confirmed` order exists per employee per meal. A racing request receives
  `409 ORDER_SLOT_CONFLICT` with the existing order in `data`.
* Both guarantees are enforced by unique indexes in MySQL, so they hold even if Redis is down or
  several application instances run in parallel.

### GET /api/orders — authenticated

My orders, newest first. `page` (default 0) and `size` (default 10, max 50).

### GET /api/orders/{id} — authenticated (owner only)

Full order detail including the option snapshot. Another employee's order returns
`403 FORBIDDEN`.

### POST /api/orders/{id}/cancel — authenticated (owner only)

Cancels a `Pending` order and releases its meal slot immediately.

* `Pending` → cancelled, `200`.
* Already `Cancelled` → `200` with the current state (idempotent).
* `Confirmed` or `Completed` → `409 ORDER_NOT_CANCELLABLE`.

---

## Console (ADMIN role required)

### GET /api/admin/dishes

| Query parameter | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `keyword` | string | ≤ 50 chars, matched against the dish name |
| `category` | string | one of the six cuisine labels |
| `available` | bool | shelf-status filter |
| `page`, `size` | int | default 0 / 10, max 50 |

Returns the same paged envelope, with each dish carrying its full option graph.

### GET /api/admin/dishes/{id}

A single dish, including option groups and options.

### POST /api/admin/dishes — `201 Created`

### PUT /api/admin/dishes/{id}

Both take the same body. `optionGroups` **replaces** the dish's option graph in one transaction.
Orders already placed are unaffected because their lines are snapshots.

```json
{
  "name": "Smoke Test Bowl",
  "description": "Dish created by the automated test",
  "price": "19.90",
  "category": "Light Meal",
  "spiceLevel": "Mild",
  "imageUrl": "/api/files/images/6f1c...e2.jpg",
  "allergens": ["Soy"],
  "proteins": ["Tofu"],
  "available": true,
  "optionGroups": [
    {
      "name": "Base",
      "required": true,
      "selectionType": "SINGLE",
      "options": [
        { "name": "Rice", "priceDelta": "0.00", "available": true },
        { "name": "Quinoa", "priceDelta": "3.00", "available": true }
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "Add-ons",
      "required": false,
      "selectionType": "MULTI",
      "options": [{ "name": "Avocado", "priceDelta": "4.00", "available": true }]
    }
  ]
}
```

Validation: name ≤ 100, description ≤ 500, price > 0 with at most 2 decimals, option names ≤ 60,
extra price ≥ 0, and a required group must contain at least one option.

### PATCH /api/admin/dishes/{id}/availability

```json
{ "available": false }
```

Taking a dish off the shelf makes it disappear from employee menus immediately (the menu cache is
invalidated in the same transaction).

### GET /api/admin/dishes/cache-stats

Menu-cache counters, useful for demonstrating the caching strategy.

```json
{ "hits": 128, "misses": 6, "fallbacks": 0, "ttlMinutes": 10 }
```

`hits` - served from Redis, `misses` - loaded from MySQL, `fallbacks` - Redis was unreachable and
MySQL served the request.

### GET /api/admin/daily-menus/{date}

Menu published for a date; an empty list when nothing is scheduled.

```json
{
  "menuDate": "2026-03-25",
  "items": [
    { "dishId": 1, "name": "Kung Pao Chicken", "category": "Chinese", "available": true,
      "totalQty": 40, "soldQty": 0, "displayOrder": 0 }
  ]
}
```

### PUT /api/admin/daily-menus/{date}

Replaces the dish list for that date, so resubmitting the same body is a no-op. Rows for dishes
that stay on the menu are updated in place, which preserves `soldQty` if today's menu is edited
mid-service.

```json
{ "items": [ { "dishId": 1, "totalQty": 40 }, { "dishId": 2, "totalQty": 25 } ] }
```

The SPA defaults the date to tomorrow and offers a "Today" shortcut, so the same screen both
schedules tomorrow and adjusts today.

### POST /api/admin/files/images

`multipart/form-data` with a single `file` field. JPG, PNG or WebP, at most 2 MB. The type is
verified from the **magic bytes**, not the declared name, and the stored name is a fresh UUID -
the original filename is discarded.

```json
{ "url": "/api/files/images/6f1c8f0e-3a1f-4d2b-9d4e-7c2f9a1b3e5d.jpg" }
```

### GET /api/files/images/{name} — public

Serves a stored image. The name must match the generated-UUID allow-list, so path traversal
attempts are rejected before the filesystem is touched.

---

## Order administration (supplement)

PRD section 1 describes the administrator as someone who manages dishes **and processes orders**,
while section 4.3 details only dish management for Tier 2. These two endpoints are the smallest
addition that honours that description and can be removed without affecting Tier 1 or Tier 2
completeness.

### GET /api/admin/orders

| Query parameter | Type | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `date` | date | filter by meal date |
| `status` | string | `Pending` / `Confirmed` / `Completed` / `Cancelled` |
| `page`, `size` | int | |

### PATCH /api/admin/orders/{id}/status

```json
{ "targetStatus": "Confirmed" }
```

Allowed transitions: `Pending → Confirmed`, `Confirmed → Completed`. `Cancelled` is accepted and
routed through the normal cancellation rule, so only `Pending` orders can be cancelled.

---

## Health and operations

| Endpoint | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /actuator/health` | readiness, including `db` and `redis` component status |
| `GET /actuator/metrics` | Micrometer metrics |
| `GET /swagger-ui.html` | interactive API documentation |
| `GET /v3/api-docs` | OpenAPI 3 document |

{"content":"# WeBox — Enterprise Employee Meal Ordering Platform

A full-stack meal ordering system for an in-house canteen. Around 200 employees browse the day's
menu on a phone or a laptop, order before the cut-off, and the kitchen prepares accordingly.
Administrators manage the dish catalog and publish each day's menu through a separate **Console**.

Built against `AI Vibe Coding V3.0 - PRD.md`: **Tier 1 (core) and Tier 2 (advanced) are complete**.
Tier 3 (real-time stock, AI recommendations, analytics dashboard) is out of scope; the extension
points are designed in and documented.

> **System language**: every user-facing string — interface, menu data, validation and error
> messages — is English, as PRD section 1 requires.

---

## Status

| Area | State |
| --- | --- |
| Backend (JDK 17 + Spring Boot 3.3 + standalone MySQL 8) | Implemented, running |
| Frontend (Vue 3 + TypeScript + Vite) | Implemented, typechecks and builds |
| Redis cache / idempotency / order numbering | Implemented, degradable |
| Unit tests (`mvn test`) | **56 passing** |
| End-to-end API checks (`scripts/smoke-test.ps1`) | **69 assertions passing** |
| Concurrency checks (`scripts/concurrency-test.ps1`) | **14 assertions passing** |
| Tier 3 | Not implemented — extension points documented |

---

## Feature scope

| Tier | Feature | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Employee registration and sign-in, session survives refresh | `/login`, `/register` |
| 1 | Daily menu with images, prices, cuisine tags, multi-select filters, search | `/` |
| 1 | Dish detail with ingredients, allergens, spice level and live-priced options | `/menu/dishes/:id` |
| 1 | Cart with per-configuration lines, quantity editing, live total | `/cart` |
| 1 | Checkout: delivery date, meal, address, single-order guarantee | `/checkout` |
| 1 | Order history, detail with option snapshot, cancellation | `/orders` |
| 2 | Dietary preferences: allergens, cuisines, spice, taste, budget | `/settings` |
| 2 | Ordering rules: 5-portion cap, cut-off auto-switch, one order per meal | checkout + menu |
| 2 | Console: dish table, create/edit with options, on/off shelf, image upload | `/console/dishes` |
| 2 | Console: set a day's menu with per-dish quantities | `/console/daily-menu` |

---

## Technology

| Layer | Choice | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Language / framework | Java 17, Spring Boot 3.3 | Required by the PRD |
| Build | Maven with the wrapper (`mvnw`) | No global Maven install needed |
| Database | **MySQL 8, standalone** | Required by the PRD; no embedded database anywhere, including tests |
| Schema | Flyway migrations | Reproducible schema; Hibernate never mutates it |

```bash

docker compose ps          # wait for webox-mysql to report healthy
```

CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS webox_test CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci;

and `WEBOX_JWT_SECRET`. If the JWT secret is empty the application generates an ephemeral one and
logs a warning — everything works, but restarting invalidates existing tokens.

zone, upload directory, cache TTL, and the seed account.

listens on `http://localhost:8080`.

npm install

the browser only ever talks to one origin.

matter:

    statuses: 200
    distinct order numbers: 1
  [PASS] all 10 responses carry the same order number
  [PASS] 9 responses were recognised as replays
  [PASS] the database holds exactly one order for that key

== Meal-slot safety: 10 different keys racing for the same meal
    status distribution: 200x1, 409x9
  [PASS] exactly one racing submit won
  [PASS] the conflict reason is ORDER_SLOT_CONFLICT
```

## Architecture in brief

```
Vue 3 SPA  ──/api──▶  Spring Boot 3.3 (JDK 17)  ──JDBC──▶  MySQL 8   (system of record)
  Pinia + TanStack Query        │                              ▲
                                └──Lettuce──▶  Redis           │ never authoritative
                                              (cache · idempotency · order numbers)
```

Four decisions carry most of the design:

1. **MySQL is the only source of truth.** Redis is a degradable accelerator; losing it costs speed,
   never correctness. The fallback is to read MySQL, deliberately not an in-process map.
2. **Concurrency is enforced by unique indexes, not by locks.** `UNIQUE(user_id, client_request_id)`
   makes submission idempotent; `UNIQUE(user_id, active_slot_key)` — where `active_slot_key` is a
   generated column that becomes NULL once an order is cancelled or completed — gives MySQL the
   equivalent of a partial unique index, so an employee can have at most one active order per meal.
   There is no distributed lock anywhere.
3. **The menu is cached as one whole-day snapshot.** It is small and read by everyone at once
   during the 09:30–10:00 peak, so one cache entry serves every concurrent reader and filtering,
   search, preference ordering and paging happen in memory. Invalidation is explicit: dish writes
   clear everything, daily-menu writes clear one date, and a 10-minute TTL is the safety net.
4. **The cart lives in the browser; the server re-derives everything.** Prices, portion limits,
   option validity, the effective meal and the duplicate-order check are all recomputed from the
   database inside the placement transaction. Nothing the client sends about money is trusted.

security design and the Tier 3 extension points.

| Client state | Pinia (auth, cart, preferences) + TanStack Query (server data) | Query gives caching and de-duplication for the busy menu endpoint |
| Styling | Tailwind CSS | Mobile-first breakpoints, which the two-device requirement needs |

Rejected alternatives and the reasoning behind each choice are recorded in
[`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) section 2.

## Getting started

### Step 1 — Start MySQL and Redis

**Option A — Docker (one command):**

```bash
docker compose up -d
docker compose ps          # wait for webox-mysql to report healthy
```

This creates the `webox` and `webox_test` schemas with user `webox` / `webox1234`.

**Option B — existing local servers:**

```sql
CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS webox      CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci;
CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS webox_test CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci;
CREATE USER IF NOT EXISTS 'webox'@'%' IDENTIFIED BY 'webox1234';
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON webox.*      TO 'webox'@'%';
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON webox_test.* TO 'webox'@'%';
FLUSH PRIVILEGES;
```

Redis needs no setup. If yours requires a password, set `WEBOX_REDIS_PASSWORD` (step 2).

> **The application does not need Redis to work.** If Redis is unreachable, the menu is read from
> MySQL, idempotency falls back to the database unique index, and order numbers use a random
> suffix. The API degrades; it does not fail.

### Step 2 — Configure

```bash
cp .env.example .env
```

Every variable has a usable localhost default except `WEBOX_DB_PASSWORD` (defaults to `webox1234`)
and `WEBOX_JWT_SECRET`. If the JWT secret is empty the application generates an ephemeral one and
logs a warning — everything works, but restarting invalidates existing tokens.

See [`.env.example`](.env.example) for the full list: database, Redis, CORS origins, business time
zone, upload directory, cache TTL, and the seed account.

### Step 3 — Start the backend

```bash
cd backend
./mvnw spring-boot:run          # Windows: .\mvnw.cmd spring-boot:run
```

On the first run Flyway creates the schema and the seeder populates the catalog. The service
listens on `http://localhost:8080`.

### Step 4 — Start the frontend

```bash
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev
```

Vite serves the SPA on `http://localhost:5173` and proxies `/api` and `/dishes` to the backend, so
the browser only ever talks to one origin.

### Step 5 — Open the app

| | URL |
| --- | --- |
| Employee app | <http://localhost:5173> |
| Console (admin) | <http://localhost:5173/console> |
| API documentation | <http://localhost:8080/swagger-ui.html> |
| Health | <http://localhost:8080/actuator/health> |

**Or start everything at once:**

```powershell
pwsh -File scripts/dev.ps1              # assumes MySQL and Redis are already running
pwsh -File scripts/dev.ps1 -WithDocker  # starts docker compose first
```
